newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE welcomes UK plans for regulatory overhaul.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE welcomes UK plans for regulatory overhaul.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE) said on Tuesday the UK Government's plans for regulatory reforms in financial services were key for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"LIFFE shares the objective set by the Chancellor of establishing a regulatory system that delivers the most effective supervision in the world," said chief executive Daniel Hobson in a statement.
"This is essential if we are to retain the UK's lead in financial services in the run-up to economic and monetary union," he said.
In a statement to Parliament on Tuesday, Brown said the government would immediately start working on the legislation needed to reform the regulatory system.
Supervision for Britain's banking sector would be transfered from the Bank of England to the Securities and Investments Board (SIB), which would become the single regulator, underpinned by statute.
The current division of responsibility between the SIB and the self regulatory organisations was inefficient and confusing for investors, Brown said.
LIFFE's Hobson welcomed the emphasis on the practitioner involvement in regulation and on differential levels of regulation for wholesale and retail business.
"This is important in achieving the right balance, which ensures effective regulation and retains scope for innovation by financial services firms," he said.
It was clear from the statement that the exchanges such as LIFFE would remain Recognised Investment Exchanges, with a regulatory role accountable to the new strengthened SIB, Hobson added.
